subject: Zephyra Dedicated: SKU empirics & memory/latency tradeoffs
messages:
From: Rachel Stern <rachel.stern@zephyra.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot sizing question — short vs long context workload

Hi Avery / Ben,

Thanks again for taking this call earlier. We're spinning up a small dedicated pilot and want to lock down the GPU SKU approach before we sign the reserve. High-level notes on our workload (CSV attached):
- Average request: 160 tokens in / 80 tokens out (short chat)
- 10% of requests are long-context retrieval + summarization: peak sequences up to 40k tokens (document chunks + prompt)
- Embedding batch jobs run off hours (3–5am PT) at ~500 concurrent embeds; modest GPU memory tolerance there
- SLO: 95th pct latency ~250ms for short requests; long-context can be best-effort but should not exceed 8s median
- Expected steady QPS: 150–250 (spiky bursts x2–3)

Primary ask: guidance on whether to push for H100 reservation (memory headroom for long-context), A100 baseline with L4 burst pool, or go L4-heavy and offload long-context to a hybrid strategy. Cost sensitivity: we want predictable unit economics for the committed months.

Can you outline recommended fleet mix and a short rationale (memory vs perf vs cost) we can present to procurement?

Attachments: zephyra_workload_profile.csv

Cheers,
Rachel
VP Product, Zephyra AI
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Stern <rachel.stern@zephyra.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-24T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing question — short vs long context workload

Rachel — thanks for the detail and the CSV. Quick read-through and a short, pragmatic approach below. I attached a one-pager (sku_empirics_note_v1.pdf) with short benchmarks and tradeoffs.

TL;DR recommendation (pilot):
- Reserve a small H100 pool sized to cover long-context sessions (10% of traffic) for RDT/low-latency long-context inference.
- Reserve A100s for the baseline short-chat workload (predictable throughput, good single-GPU throughput for medium-size prompt lengths).
- Supplement with a spare L4 burst pool for low-cost, high-concurrency short-chat bursts and background embedding jobs.

Why this split?
- Memory headroom: H100 (80GB+) gives the KV-cache and model sharding headroom for sustained 40k-token runs without heavy tiling complexity. A100-40GB will require more aggressive tiling/kv-eviction or model-splitting, which increases latency and engineering effort.
- Cost/perf: A100 provides solid token throughput at reasonable $/token for medium-context; L4 is much cheaper for short-context and embeddings but has smaller memory and may require more parallelism to hit latency SLOs.
- Operational complexity: Hybrid model routing (route long-context to H100s, short to A100/L4) is supported by Redwood's smart routing — just need clear routing rules and fallbacks.

Sizing rough (pilot baseline for 200 QPS target):
- H100 reserved: capacity to handle ~20 concurrent long-context sessions (assume 8–10s median, conservative) => 4–6 H100 GPUs depending on model and quantization.
- A100 reserved: baseline steady short-chat throughput ~160 QPS => ~8 A100-80GB equivalents (or 10x A100-40GB) depending on model/quantization.
- L4 burst pool: a handful (12–16) L4s to absorb 2–3x concurrency bursts and handle embeddings off-hours.

Next steps: if you can share expected model family (open or finetuned), target quantization (fp16/int8), and a sample token length distribution we can run a short runbook and simulated token cost vs latency profiles. Happy to run the initial bench this week.

Attachment: sku_empirics_note_v1.pdf ([attachment stub])

Best,
Avery Johnson
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Rachel Stern <rachel.stern@zephyra.ai>
Date: 2028-06-25T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing question — short vs long context workload

Looping in a quick capacity cost sketch so procurement has numbers for the pilot. See attached workbook (capacity_rational.xlsx) — top-line:
- Estimate assumptions: 200 steady QPS, 10% long-context, short-chat median = 220ms on A100-based stack with batching
- Pilot reserved commitment (3 months) cost ordering (approx):
  - H100 pool (4 GPUs): $~38k/month reserved
  - A100 pool (8 GPUs): $~24k/month reserved
  - L4 burst pool (12 GPUs, on-demand/burst): $~6–9k/month variable
- If Zephyra pushes quantization to 4-bit for the short-chat variant, A100 requirement drops by ~30% for throughput (fewer GPUs); if using int4 on H100 for long-context, memory/headroom assumptions still favor H100 due to larger VRAM.

Operational notes:
- Recommend clear routing policy in RB (route by token-count and request-tag) and an automatic fallback: if H100s are saturated, route long requests to A100s with an adaptive timeout (degrade to short summary).
- Bench plan: 48h focused perf runs (short throughput on A100 vs L4; long-context end-to-end on H100 with kv-caching enabled).

Attachments: capacity_rational.xlsx

cc: Avery for bench coordination.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Stern <rachel.stern@zephyra.ai>

Subject: Re: Pilot sizing question — short vs long context workload

Thanks — this is exactly what procurement needs. A few clarifications from our side:
- Confirmed steady QPS target: 200 (we should plan headroom for 300 during launch).
- Long-context distribution: ~10% of calls, typically multi-stage (retrieve → summarize → follow-ups) with peak token footprints up to 40k.
- Model: we'll start with a 1.3B finetuned family for short-chat and a 7B family for longcontext experiments (both quantizable).
- Budget: procurement gave us a pilot monthly budget cap; we'd prefer to minimize H100 count but not at the cost of repeated tiling and latency regressions.

Let's proceed with the proposed hybrid pilot. Can we get:
- A short mutual action plan with milestones (bench, pilot launch, telemetry review) and a 2-week window for perf runs?
- A finalized price estimate for the 3-month reserve so I can run it through procurement this week?

Happy to sync Friday for 30 minutes.

Best,
Rachel
VP Product, Zephyra AI
